verdict.rationale: Otter's own MCP Server gives AI agents OAuth-authenticated access with 'granular permissions', limiting the assistant to meetings the user explicitly authorizes. That is a first-party form of scoped, least-privilege agent access. However, the Public API uses plain API-key auth with no documented scoping, and the MCP permission model is described only in a one-line marketing blurb. missing for 10: documented scope/permission types, scoped API keys for the Public API, token lifecycle and revocation controls, per-agent credential management UI or docs, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions. Your AI assistant can only access meetings you explicitly authorize
